records.name: Rhode Island
records.summary: “Most Protective” tier in the July 2026 assessment: regional non-discrimination covering gender identity and shield/refuge protections enforceable against out-of-state actions; no state-specific negative finding beyond the shared federal layer (passport/API policy, priced into the national score). No country-unique finding beyond insurance-coverage details a visitor never encounters. Clearly above the national score 0.36.

records.name: Washington
records.summary:
A July 2026 national legal-risk map lists Washington among the federation's fifteen Most Protective states, naming it specifically for comprehensive health-insurance requirements covering gender-affirming procedures — including facial-hair removal and an expanded range of treatments — and for refuge protections for people fleeing restrictive states. Equality-map research (data as of 25 September 2026) counts Washington among the healthcare "shield"-law states that protect recipients and providers from out-of-state civil or criminal action.

Federal 2025 document and passport restrictions still apply here as across the federation.

records.name: Centro
records.summary:
The region contains two of the six regions with the highest recorded counts of anti-LGBT hate-motivated violence in the 2012-2025 region-by-region study maintained by the country's principal LGBT monitoring project.

Against that stands the strongest judicial response to transphobic violence recorded anywhere in the country: in January 2025 a first-instance court in this region's main university city recognised a "transphobic motive" in the punitive rape of a trans sex worker, sentenced the perpetrator, awarded damages to the victim and to the association that supports trans sex workers, and - for the first time - admitted the national trans-movement organisation as civil party.

For a visitor the combination is specific: the highest-frequency regions of the country's violence record are here, but so is a documented court that named transphobic motive and ordered reparation.

records.name: Nord-Ovest
records.summary:
This region hosts the country's first and second practical civic gender-recognition schemes: Milano's "registro di genere" - chosen name on civic and municipal documents, public-transport subscriptions and staff badges, created by a 2022 council motion brought by the country's first elected transgender councillor - and Torino's analogous "Identita Alias" practice at the municipality and the public libraries. For a gender-nonconforming visitor these determine whether a ticket window or municipal desk becomes an argument.

Against this, the 2012-2025 region-by-region study of anti-LGBT hate-motivated violence names this region's two leading regions among the country's six highest-victim regions.

records.name: Nord-Est
records.summary:
The region's dominant constituent authority carries a documented record of official acts of hostility toward trans people. In 2014, following a council deliberation, the regional government formally instituted a mandatory "Natural Family Day" on the last school day before the Christmas holidays and rejected the aims and content of the WHO Regional Office's Standards for Sexuality Education in Europe, committing to deploy every available instrument against their adoption in the region's schools (official regional bulletin, December 2014).

In July 2018 the regional council approved a further motion pledging support for "those who fight in defence of the natural family" and for natalist policies, attacking the civil-unions law, and dismissing Pride marches as "carnival farces". These official acts create a clearly unwelcome climate signal; neither imposes a criminal sanction, fine or enforcement exposure on a visitor.

records.name: Sud
records.summary:
The state's principal international LGBT-rights federation's annual country review (February 2025) finds a troubling increase in the number and geographic spread of bias-motivated violence against LGBTI people, with incidents reported almost monthly - and includes in that finding a March 2025 scooter-mounted homophobic assault on a young man in this region's largest metropolitan periphery.

In October 2025 at a commuter railway station in the region's main metropolitan area an activist - president of a local LGBT association - was subjected to an escalating verbal homophobic attack ending in threats of stabbing by two young men. The station setting is one any visitor could occupy. The underlying local-newspaper report was bot-blocked at fetch time; it is retained as a sourced event on the strength of the recorded claim.

records.name: Isole
records.summary:
At roughly 5 a.m. on 26 April 2025 three young men were beaten in a fast-food restaurant in this region's largest city solely because they were gay; the victims were hospitalised, video of the attack later circulated publicly, and the prosecutor's office reconstructed the sequence - insults and threats first, then the physical assault.

A June 2026 press survey of reporting from the island documents a sustained pattern rather than isolated events: rising homophobic bullying, violence against LGBTIA+ people and associated suicides, with multiple cases listed. The pattern is qualitative but official: a hospitalisation-level public assault and an prosecutorial reconstruction sit alongside a growing documented toll.
